templates.pattern: A plant cell has a solute potential of [SP] kPa and a pressure potential of [PP] kPa. Calculate the water potential of the cell in kPa.
templates.explanation:
Water potential ψ = solute potential + pressure potential
= ψs + ψp
= −[SP] + [PP]
= [RESULT] kPa

Solute potential is always negative — solutes lower water potential. Pressure potential is usually positive in turgid plant cells. Water moves from higher to lower water potential.

templates.pattern: A substance diffuses across a membrane with a surface area of [SA] μm², a concentration difference of [CD] mmol/L and a membrane thickness of [T] μm. Calculate the rate of diffusion in arbitrary units.
templates.explanation:
Rate of diffusion = (surface area × concentration difference) ÷ thickness
= ([SA] × [CD]) ÷ [T]
= [SA*CD] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT]

Fick's Law: diffusion rate increases with surface area and concentration gradient but decreases with membrane thickness. This explains why exchange surfaces are thin and highly folded.

templates.pattern: A person has a heart rate of [HR] beats per minute and a stroke volume of [SV] mL per beat. Calculate the cardiac output in mL per minute.
templates.explanation:
Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume
= [HR] × [SV]
= [RESULT] mL/min

Resting cardiac output is about 5000 mL/min. During exercise it can reach 20,000-25,000 mL/min in trained athletes. Both heart rate and stroke volume increase during exercise.

templates.pattern: A microscope slide shows [TOTAL] cells in a field of view. [MIT] cells are observed in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
templates.explanation:
Mitotic index = (cells in mitosis ÷ total cells) × 100
= ([MIT] ÷ [TOTAL]) × 100
= [RESULT]%

A high mitotic index indicates rapid cell division — seen in growing tissues and tumours. Cancer cells have abnormally high mitotic indices. Normal skin has a mitotic index of about 5-10%.

templates.pattern: A bacterial population doubles every [T] minutes. Starting from 1 cell calculate the time taken to produce [N] doublings in minutes.
templates.explanation:
Time for n doublings = n × doubling time
= [N] × [T]
= [RESULT] minutes

Doubling time is the time for a population to double. E. coli doubles every 20 minutes under ideal conditions. Human cells take about 24 hours to divide.

templates.pattern: A bacterial population starts with [P0] cells and undergoes [N] doublings. Calculate the final population size.
templates.explanation:
Final population = initial population × 2ⁿ
= [P0] × 2^[N]
= [P0] × [pow(2,N)]
= [RESULT]

Exponential bacterial growth can produce enormous populations very quickly. Starting from just 1 cell after 40 doublings there would be over 1 trillion cells.

templates.pattern: A cell produces [CO2] molecules of CO₂ and consumes [O2] molecules of O₂ during respiration. Calculate the respiratory quotient (RQ).
templates.explanation:
Respiratory quotient = CO₂ produced ÷ O₂ consumed
= [CO2] ÷ [O2]
= [RESULT]

RQ = 1.0 for carbohydrates, 0.7 for fats and 0.8 for proteins. A mixed diet gives RQ ≈ 0.85. RQ can exceed 1.0 during anaerobic respiration when CO₂ is produced without O₂ being consumed.

templates.pattern: A plant has a gross photosynthesis rate of [GROSS] μmol CO₂/m²/s and a respiration rate of [RESP] μmol CO₂/m²/s. Calculate the net photosynthesis rate in μmol CO₂/m²/s.
templates.explanation:
Net photosynthesis = gross photosynthesis − respiration
= [GROSS] − [RESP]
= [RESULT] μmol CO₂/m²/s

Net photosynthesis is the carbon actually fixed by the plant after its own respiratory needs are met. At the compensation point net photosynthesis = 0.

templates.pattern: A spherical cell has a radius of [R] μm. Calculate the surface area of the cell in μm².
templates.explanation:
Surface area of sphere = 4πr²
= 4 × π × [R]²
= 4 × 3.14159 × [R*R]
= [RESULT] μm²

Most cells are approximately spherical. The surface area determines the rate of exchange of gases, nutrients and waste products with the surrounding environment.

templates.pattern: Cells in mitosis are observed for [MIT_DUR] minutes. The mitotic index of the tissue is [MI]%. Calculate the total cell cycle length in minutes.
templates.explanation:
Cell cycle length = mitosis duration × 100 ÷ mitotic index
= [MIT_DUR] × 100 ÷ [MI]
= [RESULT] minutes

If 10% of cells are in mitosis at any time and mitosis takes 60 minutes then the full cell cycle takes 600 minutes = 10 hours.
